reading.title: The Rise and Fall of the Minoan Civilization
reading.passage: The Minoan civilization, flourishing on the island of Crete from approximately 3000 to 1100 BCE, represents one of antiquity's most sophisticated societies. Archaeological evidence reveals that Minoans developed an advanced system of writing, constructed elaborate palaces with sophisticated plumbing systems, and engaged in extensive maritime trade throughout the Mediterranean. Their economic prosperity stemmed primarily from agricultural production and commercial exchange, enabling them to accumulate considerable wealth and cultural refinement. However, the civilization's decline remains a subject of scholarly debate. While some researchers attribute the collapse to a catastrophic volcanic eruption on the nearby island of Thera around 1600 BCE, others argue that gradual environmental degradation and subsequent invasions by Mycenaean Greeks precipitated the civilization's demise. The archaeological record indicates that following the volcanic catastrophe, Minoan settlements experienced significant destruction, yet recovery occurred in subsequent centuries. Nevertheless, by 1100 BCE, the distinctive Minoan culture had been assimilated into the emerging Mycenaean civilization, effectively terminating the Bronze Age Aegean's most enigmatic culture.

questions.q: According to the passage, what was the primary source of Minoan economic wealth?
options: Military conquests and territorial expansion
Agricultural production and commercial exchange
Mining of precious metals and gemstones
Religious taxation and temple tributes
questions.explanation: 지문의 두 번째 문장에서 'Their economic prosperity stemmed primarily from agricultural production and commercial exchange'라고 명시하고 있습니다.

questions.q: What can be inferred from the passage about the cause of the Minoan civilization's decline?
options: There is a single, universally accepted explanation for its collapse
Scholars disagree about whether the volcanic eruption was the sole cause
Environmental degradation was the only significant factor
The Mycenaean invasion occurred before the volcanic eruption
questions.explanation: 지문에서 '의견이 분분하다'는 'remains a subject of scholarly debate'와 'While some researchers...others argue' 표현으로 학자들 간의 의견 불일치를 명확히 보여줍니다.

questions.q: The word 'precipitated' in the third sentence is closest in meaning to
options: delayed or postponed
caused or triggered
predicted or forecasted
documented or recorded
questions.explanation: 'precipitated'는 '촉발하다', '야기하다'는 의미의 동사로, 여기서는 '야기했다'는 뜻입니다. 즉 'caused or triggered'가 가장 가까운 의미입니다.

questions.q: Why does the author mention the sophisticated plumbing systems in Minoan palaces?
options: To explain why the civilization was destroyed by water damage
To support the claim that Minoans possessed advanced engineering knowledge
To contrast Minoan technology with later Greek civilizations
To indicate that Minoans had developed written records
questions.explanation: 저자는 정교한 배관 시스템을 언급함으로써 미노아 문명의 발전된 기술 수준과 정교함을 입증하려고 합니다. 이는 '가장 정교한 사회 중 하나'라는 주제 문장을 뒷받침합니다.

sentences.original: The Minoan civilization, flourishing on the island of Crete from approximately 3000 to 1100 BCE, represents one of antiquity's most sophisticated societies.
sentences.paraphrase: One of the ancient world's most advanced civilizations, the Minoan culture thrived on Crete for roughly three millennia, between 3000 and 1100 BCE.
sentences.tip: 복잡한 앞치사 구문을 주어로 이동하고, 시간 표현을 다시 표현하여 문장 구조 변환

sentences.original: Their economic prosperity stemmed primarily from agricultural production and commercial exchange, enabling them to accumulate considerable wealth and cultural refinement.
sentences.paraphrase: Because Minoans depended chiefly on farming and trade for their economic success, they were able to gather abundant riches and achieve high cultural standards.
sentences.tip: 명사구(economic prosperity stemmed from)를 인과 접속사(Because)를 사용한 절로 변환하고 동의어로 치환

sentences.original: While some researchers attribute the collapse to a catastrophic volcanic eruption on the nearby island of Thera around 1600 BCE, others argue that gradual environmental degradation and subsequent invasions by Mycenaean Greeks precipitated the civilization's demise.
sentences.paraphrase: Scholars present competing theories: some blame a massive volcanic explosion on Thera near 1600 BCE for ending the civilization, whereas others contend that slow ecological deterioration combined with Mycenaean military conquest caused its downfall.
sentences.tip: 양보절 구문(While...others)을 동등 절(Scholars present theories: some...whereas others) 구조로 재구성하고 어휘 단순화

sentences.original: The archaeological record indicates that following the volcanic catastrophe, Minoan settlements experienced significant destruction, yet recovery occurred in subsequent centuries.
sentences.paraphrase: Evidence from excavations shows that although the volcano caused widespread damage to Minoan communities, these settlements were reconstructed over the following centuries.
sentences.tip: 능동 구문 유지하되, 'yet recovery occurred'를 능동 동사 'were reconstructed'로 변환하여 흐름 개선

sentences.original: Nevertheless, by 1100 BCE, the distinctive Minoan culture had been assimilated into the emerging Mycenaean civilization, effectively terminating the Bronze Age Aegean's most enigmatic culture.
sentences.paraphrase: By the year 1100 BCE, however, the unique Minoan way of life had been absorbed by the rising Mycenaean society, thereby ending what was perhaps the Bronze Age Mediterranean's most mysterious civilization.
sentences.tip: 수동태 유지하고, 부사(distinctly→unique)와 명사(enigmatic culture→mysterious civilization)로 어휘 다양화

speaking.prompt: Some people believe students should freely choose their major based on personal interest and passion. Others think students should pursue majors that offer better job prospects and financial security. Which position do you agree with more, and why? Please provide specific reasons and examples to support your answer.
model_sentences: I personally believe that students should prioritize choosing a major based on their genuine interests rather than purely job market considerations.
First, when students study subjects they're passionate about, they're naturally more motivated and tend to perform better academically, which ultimately leads to stronger job prospects anyway.

For example, my friend Sarah chose psychology because she was genuinely fascinated by understanding human behavior, even though her parents suggested business; her enthusiasm led her to excel in her courses, and she was actually recruited by a top consulting firm because of her excellent grades and research experience.
Additionally, pursuing your passion makes your career more fulfilling and sustainable long-term, since you'll spend decades in your profession.
In conclusion, while job market demand matters, I believe that choosing a major aligned with your interests creates a better foundation for both academic success and career satisfaction.

listening.title: Psychology Lecture: The Formation of Memory
listening.script: Professor: Good morning, everyone. Today we're going to discuss how memories are actually formed in our brains. This is a fascinating process. So, let's start with the basic concept: memory formation involves three key stages. First, there's encoding, which is when your brain takes in new information and converts it into a form that can be stored. This happens through sensory perception. Next comes consolidation, where the brain literally reorganizes and stabilizes these encoded memories, often through sleep and repetition. This is why cramming the night before an exam isn't ideal—your brain needs time to consolidate. Finally, there's retrieval, which is simply recalling the information when you need it. Now, here's something important: the hippocampus, a small region deep in your brain, plays a crucial role in consolidating new memories into long-term storage. Research has shown that damage to the hippocampus severely impairs the ability to form new memories. However, interestingly, long-term memories that were already formed before the injury remain relatively intact. This tells us that once memories are consolidated and distributed throughout the cortex, they don't depend on the hippocampus anymore. Any questions so far?

vocabulary.meaning_ko: 정보를 저장 가능한 형태로 변환하는 과정
뇌의 해마 부위 (기억 형성에 중요한 역할)

questions.q: According to the professor, what is the main function of encoding in memory formation?
options: To stabilize memories through sleep and repetition
To convert new information into a storable form through sensory perception
To retrieve stored memories when needed
To reorganize memories in the hippocampus
questions.explanation: 교수는 강의에서 'encoding, which is when your brain takes in new information and converts it into a form that can be stored'라고 명시했습니다.

questions.q: Why does the professor mention that cramming the night before an exam isn't ideal?
options: Because students won't have time to attend class
Because the brain needs time to consolidate memories, which cramming doesn't allow
Because the hippocampus is less active at night
Because encoding is impossible without proper sleep
questions.explanation: 교수는 consolidation 단계를 설명하며 'your brain needs time to consolidate. This is why cramming the night before an exam isn't ideal'라고 직접 언급했습니다.

questions.q: What does the professor imply about memories after they have been consolidated and distributed throughout the cortex?
options: They become more dependent on the hippocampus
They can be retrieved more quickly but become less accurate
They no longer require the hippocampus for storage and recall
They are vulnerable to being lost during sleep
questions.explanation: 교수는 'once memories are consolidated and distributed throughout the cortex, they don't depend on the hippocampus anymore'라고 명시적으로 설명했습니다.
